q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of plastic toys?
title: Plastic toy carbon footprint per kg
short: Weigh each polymer in the toy, such as ABS, PP or PVC, and multiply by its supplier's per-kg figure. Add moulding, assembly, painting and packing energy, divide plant energy by kg passed, and add batteries or electronics separately.
audience: Toy makers, including Delhi NCR and Mumbai units

ul: ABS, PP, PE or PVC by weight per toy, plus runners not reground.
Batteries, motors and circuit boards for electronic toys.
Window boxes, blister packs and cartons, often heavier than expected.

p: Report per kg for a range and per piece for a buyer's SKU. Packaging can be a large share for small toys.

example.title: Worked example: toy factory per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 42,600 / 40,000 = 1.065 kg CO2 per kg
Add polymers, paint and packaging for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
